ALGER, 14/07/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Le mi: ALGIERS, 07/14/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announces the launch of a national campaign aimed at generalizing the adoption of the IPv6 protocol in Algeria. This initiative is part of the 2030 digital plan and aims to modernize the country's telecommunications infrastructure.
Généralisation du protocole IPv6 : une p: Generalization of the IPv6 protocol: a national priority for the Algerian internet infrastructure
Le ministère de la Poste et des Télécomm: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications has launched a national campaign to accelerate the adoption of the IPv6 protocol, marking a key step in the modernization of telecommunications infrastructure in Algeria. This initiative, presented during a technical meeting held in Algiers, aims to guarantee stable and secure internet connectivity for 30 million national users. According to the latest data from ARPCE, only 15% of equipment in Algeria currently uses the IPv6 protocol, compared to 40% globally. The ministry has set an ambitious target: reaching 50% adoption by the end of 2027, with full generalization planned for 2030.
La transition vers l’IPv6 s’avère crucia: The transition to IPv6 is proving crucial to respond to the exponential growth in internet traffic, estimated at 40% per year in Algeria. This protocol, which makes it possible to allocate 340 billion IP addresses (compared to 4.3 billion for IPv4), resolves the problem of address shortage and improves the quality of services offered by national operators, notably Algérie Télécom, Mobilis SA and Djezzy. During the meeting, the minister stressed that this transition will be accompanied by a strengthening of the technical capacities of the wilayas and municipalities, with a budget of 2 billion dinars allocated to local infrastructure.
La généralisation de l’IPv6 représente u: The generalization of IPv6 represents a strategic lever for the Algerian digital economy. By 2027, the e-commerce, online banking and government services sectors are expected to benefit from faster and more secure connectivity, reducing the costs of managing IPv4 addresses. According to an ANPT study, this transition could generate savings of 15 billion dinars per year by optimizing the use of network resources. Furthermore, the massive adoption of IPv6 will facilitate the integration of emerging technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), estimated at 50 billion connected devices by 2030.
Sur le plan technologique, la migration: On a technological level, migration to IPv6 improves the quality of service for operators by reducing latencies and increasing the stability of connections. For citizens, this will result in a better user experience, particularly in rural areas where internet coverage remains patchy. The ministry also announced the establishment of an awareness program in the 58 wilayas, involving the APCs (Communal Popular Assemblies) and the daïras to support individuals and businesses in this transition.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
L’Algérie compte aujourd’hui plus de 30: Algeria today has more than 30 million internet subscribers, with a mobile penetration rate exceeding 120% in 2025, according to ARPCE data. The telecommunications sector represents an annual turnover of 300 billion dinars, with average growth of 8% per year. The 2030 digital plan, led by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, provides for investments of 1,000 billion dinars to modernize infrastructure, including 300 billion dedicated to high-speed networks and the generalization of IPv6.
L’ARPCE (Autorité de Régulation de la Po: The ARPCE (Regulatory Authority for Postal and Electronic Communications) plays a central role in regulating and supervising this transition. Since 2024, the authority has required operators (Algérie Télécom, Mobilis SA, Djezzy and Ooredoo) to reserve 30% of their bandwidth for IPv6 compatible services. Furthermore, Algérie Télécom, market leader with 18 million subscribers, has already deployed 5,000 km of IPv6 compatible optical fibers in the main wilayas, including Algiers, Oran and Constantine.
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Mr. Karim Bibi Triki, declared: “The generalization of IPv6 is an absolute priority for Algeria. We work closely with operators and local authorities to ensure a smooth and inclusive transition. This initiative is part of our vision of a competitive and resilient digital economy. » The CEO of Mobilis SA, Mr. Yacine Ouali, added: “Mobilis SA is committed to supporting this transition by modernizing its network and training its technical teams. We are aiming for 100% IPv6 coverage by 2028.”
La campagne de généralisation de l’IPv6: The IPv6 generalization campaign will take place in three phases. The first, planned for the third quarter of 2026, will concern the most densely populated wilayas, such as Algiers, Oran and Blida. The second phase, planned for 2027, will target medium-sized wilayas, while full generalization is scheduled for 2030. The ministry will collaborate with operators to organize training sessions in the country's 1,541 municipalities, with particular emphasis on rural areas.
Parallèlement, l’ARPCE finalisera d’ici: At the same time, the ARPCE will finalize by the end of 2026 a reinforced regulatory framework to impose IPv6 compatibility on new connected equipment (smartphones, routers, etc.). This measure aims to accelerate the spontaneous adoption of the protocol by users. Finally, a fund of 500 million dinars will be allocated to Algerian startups specializing in IoT and cloud solutions, in order to stimulate innovation around IPv6 compatible technologies.
